# Pragma Research

> Cadence is a novel real-time AI modeled after animal and human brains. It learns from live experience.

Most of today's AI runs on transformers, which are completely feed-forward and are typically deployed with their attention matrices and all other weights fixed once training ends. Cadence runs in real time and keeps learning from each action and its result. Pragma Research builds the brains for robots that keep improving throughout their working lives. Robotics is the first proposed market. The product direction is a supported Cadence runtime and a brain prepared for a customer's embodiment, beginning with a paid evaluation on one adaptation or recovery task.

Cadence 0.71.0 builds one continuing brain. System 1 is the default: perception, plastic connections, a working trace, associative memory, action and private imagination, learning from the measured outcome of each action with no separate training mode. System 2 is optional: observing regions read the brain's own activity and return feedback inside the same settlement. Bounded observer-like, self-reading patches carry local state and records, receive signals through ports, and repair their disagreement together; the settled state supplies the answer. A layout whose patches never settle against one another does not build.

- [Compared with deep learning](https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#deep-networks): a settled equilibrium of the whole brain and local repair, beside a one-pass network trained by backpropagation.
- [Compared with deep learning](https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#deep-networks): a settled equilibrium of the whole brain and local repair, beside a one-pass network trained by backpropagation.

- [CartPole evidence excerpt](https://floatingpragma.io/evidence/cadence/cartpole-confirmations.json): 180 held-out episodes at the 500-step limit with supplied-state teaching.

Simulation evidence establishes bounded behavior under the stated conditions. Physical robot adaptation, a useful advantage from recursive depth, broad retention and electrical energy advantages require separate tests. Evidence excerpts are compact source projections, not complete reproduction bundles.

## Research origin

Observer Patch Holography (OPH) asks whether bounded observers can build a shared physical account from local records, overlap comparison and repair. Its organizing idea inspired Cadence; cortical cooperation supplies another computational inspiration. Formal proofs establish consequences of specified assumptions. A physical or biological interpretation requires its own evidence.

- [Research overview](https://floatingpragma.io/physics/).
- [Research explainer](https://floatingpragma.io/watch/).

- [Physics preprint](https://philpapers.org/rec/MUEFOC).
- [Pragma Research Blog](https://blog.floatingpragma.io/).
- [Scientific source](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/).
- [Extended source map](https://floatingpragma.io/llms-full.txt).

## Advantages for embodied AI

Animal and human brains learn from experience and not by backpropagation with gradient descent. Cadence is designed the same way: its connections change locally while the brain keeps running. For a robot or another embodied system this gives:

- Learning on the job: the same brain acts and learns from every measured outcome, with no training phase before deployment and no difference between training and inference.
- Adaptation to changed conditions: a worn actuator, a new payload or a different surface shows up in what the robot measures, and the live brain adjusts without being told what changed.
- Local learning: each connection changes from the activity of the two units it joins; the default brain keeps no backward computation graph, so learning can run on the robot itself.
- Memory: a working trace carries the recent past and an associative memory keeps what mattered.
- Settled answers: every action is the settled state of the whole brain, and a brain that does not settle refuses to act.
- Inspection: the activity of every region can be read while the brain runs, and private imagination tests a response before the body commits to it.

These properties are shown in simulation (Rover Lab, Patch World, Atari Arcade). Cadence 0.71 is experimental research software; a physical robot evaluation is the next test. Under idealized conditions the local learning contrast follows the gradient that backpropagation would compute; the comparison is of update mechanisms.

## Compared with a deep neural network

A feed-forward deep network computes an answer in one pass from input to output and is trained by backpropagation, which carries an error measured at the output backwards through every layer. A Cadence brain reaches its answer by settling: its parts are connected in both directions, each patch repairs its own disagreement with its neighbours, and the equilibrium of the whole brain is the answer, a consensus reached through local repair alone. Learning is the same process: an outcome disturbs the equilibrium, the patches repair the disagreement, the connections involved change from local activity, and the brain settles into a new equilibrium. Cadence brains can be deep; more layers join the same settlement and the learning stays local. Full comparison: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence#how-a-cadence-brain-differs-from-a-feed-forward-network

Full comparison: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence#how-a-cadence-brain-differs-from-a-feed-forward-network

## Brain design: System 1 and optional System 2

System 1 is the default brain, composed with Brain.compose; System 2 adds optional observers to the same brain. Every answer is the settled state of the whole brain, and a brain that does not settle refuses to act. Beside the main interface, Cadence 0.71.0 keeps advanced engines with their own contracts: the population solver, where populations of patches settle one joint energy and observers read exact prediction errors; record patches for event records and consolidation; and a temporal model for learned action consequences and planning. System 1 and System 2 name functional roles in software, not claims of biological equivalence. Choose observers by measured task quality, query latency and learning cost; deeper is not automatically better or faster. Archived AMEN uses a record-patch brain trained on an earlier release.

## Public demonstrations

The official demonstration source is https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos. The website showcase is https://floatingpragma.io/demos/.

- Atari Arcade: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/atari-arcade/ — a playable browser edition in which fresh Cadence brains learn Freeway and Atlantis from a scripted teacher and rewards, on an Atari 2600 emulator with a JavaScript version of the Cadence 0.70 System 1 brain; the Python server edition with four games is at https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/atari-arcade.
- AMEN: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/amen/ — a playable record-patch composer trained on Cadence 0.70; fixed learned checkpoint, generated musical events and supplied instrument.
- Patch World: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/patch-world/ — a playable JavaScript artificial-life simulation on the Cadence 0.70 population solver: brains that learn in the browser and evolve their layouts, with observer stages as an optional gene.
- Rover Lab: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/rover-lab/ — a playable browser edition of a simulated rover whose live body model adapts when a wheel weakens, with no separate training mode: a four-patch brain on a JavaScript version of the Cadence 0.70 population solver, a supplied action selector and declared timing measurements; the Python edition on cadence-net 0.70.0, with an optional observer arm, is at https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/rover-lab.

The embedded browser applications are copied from a pinned cadence-demos commit; their source and published file hashes are at https://floatingpragma.io/demos/runtime/manifest.json. Their engines differ, so the showcase identifies each mechanism and result separately.
